Sophia's Gymnastics Adventure

Stronger skills, smart practice, new goals

    Class days are examples. Your coach decides what you practice, and you can always do less if you're tired.

    Make familiar moves look fantastic

    • Beautiful lines: pointed toes, straight legs, tall posture, graceful arms.
    • Better balance: steady poses on the floor first, then the beam with your coach.
    • Confident finishes: end every move in control and hold the pose for two seconds.

    My skills

    Tap a skill's button to move it along: Want to learn → Practicing → Got it!

    My four-week goal

    • Get stronger at backbend and back walkover basics.
    • Be more steady at one handspring step my coach picks.
    • Polish a short routine using skills I already know.

    I don't have to learn a new trick in four weeks to succeed.

    My seven missions

    Creativity challenge

    Make a floor routine with 3 to 5 parts using moves you've mastered: an opening pose, a cartwheel, a balance, a dance step, and a finish. Pick music if you like. Show your coach before you perform it.

    Once a month, with permission, record your routine and compare it to the last one. Look for smoother moves, better balance, and more confidence.

    My gymnastics journal

    Practice felt

    Smart gymnast rules

    • Warm up before training.
    • Never force a stretch that hurts.
    • Try new or hard skills only with your coach, spotting, and mats.
    • Tell a grown-up or coach if something hurts, especially wrists, back, or shoulders.
    • Celebrate little improvements.
    • Get good sleep and rest days.

    My reminder

    Great gymnastics isn't about learning tricks fast. It's practicing smart, noticing progress, listening to my body and my coach, and having fun.
